ECE 6390 / Antennas and arrays

Usable band

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows the separate electrical-size, surface-precision and range checks used for a reflector model.

Electrical size compares the largest aperture dimension D with wavelength λ = c/f. A supplied class screening rule uses D of roughly five wavelengths or more for a large-aperture approximation.

Surface precision concerns residual error from the intended reflector shape. The illustrative λ/8 rule concerns that residual, while mesh openings represent another physical length. These screening rules are not exact efficiency formulas.

The chosen Fraunhofer screen rF = 2D²/λ grows with aperture size squared and frequency. It checks field-region assumptions separately from feed bandwidth, material losses, or pointing accuracy.

Example

For D = 2 m and λ = 0.03 m, the stated far-field screen is approximately 267 m. A 1 mm surface residual is smaller than λ/8 = 3.75 mm.

Model and course sources

    Practice

    1. At fixed physical aperture and surface error, what changes in the far-field distance and λ/8 tolerance when frequency doubles?

    Doubling frequency halves wavelength.

    The chosen far-field distance doubles, while the allowed λ/8 residual halves. Higher frequency makes both screens more demanding.
